title: When the Weight Doesn't Lift
subtitle: For grief that has outlasted everyone's patience — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For the reader carrying a loss the world expected them to be over by now, and for anyone sitting beside them with nothing to say.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Begin in the dark where grief actually lives — Saturday, the empty room, the God who seems to have stepped out — before any word about morning.

items.label: When Grief Doesn't Lift
items.blurb: Some griefs do not resolve. They are carried. The church should say so.

items.label: Where Is God When You're Grieving?
items.blurb: The silence in the empty room is the oldest complaint in the Psalms.

items.label: Where Is God on Holy Saturday?
items.blurb: The day between the cross and the tomb is the one most of us actually live in.

items.label: Why Christian Hope Is Not Wishful Thinking
items.blurb: Hope that skips the grave is sentiment. This one goes through it.

movements.heading: Then walk it, a week at a time
movements.note: Eight Weeks of Walking With Loss is a guided grief companion — permission to mourn, lament as a language, and a way to live forward without leaving them behind. Keep real help close; it points the way.

items.label: Eight Weeks of Walking With Loss — a grief companion
items.blurb: An eight-week plan you work at your own pace, alone or beside someone.

movements.heading: Then read the book, free
movements.note: Hard Questions gathers the long-form work on suffering, evil, the hiddenness of God, and whether faith survives them. The full book, free.

items.label: Hard Questions — read free
items.blurb: Twenty-two chapters of honest answers for a skeptical age. Free to read in full.

items.label: Find James's books in the bookstore
items.blurb: Print and ebook editions of the full library.
